text:
maria: Heads-up — ran a profile on the private VPC serving cluster and saw a regression in token-level tail latency after the kernel-selection changes. Putting the perf dump here for context.
noah: ugh, is this on Dedicated or Private?
maria: Private (air-gapped customer VPC). The regression shows up only when KV cache hits are >70% and batching is small (1-4).
sam: can you paste the p95/p99 numbers?
maria: p95 token latency went from 9ms -> 15ms, p99 from 42ms -> 94ms for hot prefixes. Overall per-request generation latency smaller but token-level really spiking.
dinesh: any correlation with kernel selector logs? maybe selected a fallback kernel that is slower for small batches.
maria: yes — kernel-selector log shows we fell back to int8_compat path for several layers; CPU-side overhead from kernel dispatch grew. Patch we rolled last week changed heuristic: prefer quant kernels for memory but didn't cost in dispatch overhead.
elaine: interesting. Does this happen only in air-gapped envs?
maria: it manifested there because the customer's Prometheus scrape is via our scrape-proxy (we push aggregated metrics), so we only saw the token-breakdown after enabling the proxy aggregation. For hosted clusters we had earlier rollout with no regression.
noah: wait — are we sure telemetry isn't missing in the private deploy so kernels are mis-ranked on cold-start?
maria: telemetry was reduced due to privacy settings in the private deploy; kernel selector uses local micro-profiles. The micro-profiles were truncated because the profiler daemon couldn't upload traces to central storage (air-gap). That made the selector use fallback cost estimates.
sam: so two issues: (1) profiler telemetry truncation in air-gapped env -> suboptimal kernel selection; (2) metrics plumbing for per-token breakdown via scratch exporter.
dinesh: for the air-gap case we talked about a scraping proxy that runs in the customer VPC and then ships compressed snapshots out-of-band. Is that live?
maria: customer uses our scrape-proxy microservice but it's running in push mode to a secure S3 bucket. ops-bot: deploy request accepted for scrape-proxy v0.3 -> staging.
elaine: we should avoid any heuristics that rely on central uploads. Kernel selector needs a local estimator that doesn't require full telemetry. Maybe run a fast local microbench during deploy to rank kernels.
oah: agree. We have a lightweight kernel-benchmark step (30s) we can run on first boot. It currently is disabled on private by default due to noise. Can toggle to opt-in via config.
sam: also need dashboards: token-level latency breakdown per-route so customers + SEs can see hot-prefix vs model-init cost. Right now Private exports only high-level request latency.
maria: attaching the mini grafana panel config I'm prototyping. snippet: 
```
- expr: sum(rate(tokens_latency_bucket[5m])) by (route,le)
  labels:
    panel: token_latency_hist
```

noah: in air-gapped setups, we can't rely on live Prometheus scraping. Options: (A) run a local Prometheus + Grafana stack in customer VPC (bigger footprint) (B) run our scrape-proxy that aggregates and uploads encrypted metrics snapshots (C) pushgateway-like pattern per-route aggregated counters.
dinesh: (B) is what they asked for. But we need to guarantee no PII leakage and keep size small. Suggest: send summaries every 5m, include token breakdown histograms + per-route throughput/errs. Compressed protobuf.
maria: proto schema v2 ready. But we need to wire in the token-level histogram collection in runtime — currently histograms are per-request latency only. Need token-level buckets emitted at token emit points.
elaine: that's more instrumentation work but doable. Keep bucket count small (10 buckets) and expose counts per-route and per-model.
sam: dashboard design note: per-route KPIs -> tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 token latency, cache-hit-rate, mean-batch-size, kernel-path (most-used). Kernel-path would be a label value we can annotate.
oah: how will kernel-path be represented? as string label on samples? careful — cardinality risk. Maybe expose top-k kernel paths per-minute as a separate metric with small dimension.
dinesh: agree limit labels. We'll emit a gauge with the top kernel id + count for that minute.
maria: action items: (1) Sam + Maria add token-level histogram emission in runtime (PR) — target EOD Thursday. (2) Noah enable boot micro-benchmark in private default but gated behind feature flag (opt-out). (3) Dinesh implement compressed snapshot upload from scrape-proxy and add encryption. (4) Elaine prototype Grafana dashboard panels for per-route KPIs.
ops-bot: reminder: please file RFC for telemetry changes and privacy review before enabling push from customer VPC.
sam: I'll open the dashboard PR after the runtime PR lands. Maria — can you paste the profiler trace here for the kernel dispatch hot path?
maria: pasted gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/profiler-kerneldispatch-176999
noah: thanks. Quick mitigation we can do: change kernel-selector to prefer kernels with lower dispatch overhead when mean-batch-size < 8. That should restore token tail while we fix telemetry.
maria: agreed — I'll draft the rollback/guard in a small PR and run it in staging.
dinesh: and for release notes we should call out the air-gapped telemetry opt-in and the new scrape-proxy schema.
elaine: +1. Also include sample Grafana JSON so customers can import.
maria: will coordinate with security to get the privacy signoff. Thanks all :thumbsup:
